newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to visit Mexico, Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to visit Mexico, Latin America.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will visit Mexico April 11-12 and make a separate trip to Barbados, Costa Rica, Brazil and Argentina in May, the White House said on Wednesday.
"The president will travel to Mexico April 11 through 12," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said. The trip to the Caribbean and South America will take place May 6-13, he added.

McCurry said Clinton would meet Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo during his April trip and discuss economic issues associated with the implementation of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), as well as immigration, fighting drug trafficking and environmental protection.

He said Clinton considered Mexico a close neighbor and partner and the United States had "a very direct interest in the recovery of the Mexican economy." McCurry added "the president put some major political capital on the line" to help Mexico recover.

In his State of the Union speech to Congress on Tuesday evening, Clinton hailed the success of his controversial economic rescue package for Mexico. The president noted that Mexico has repaid all the money it borrowed from Washington and that U.S. exports to its southern neighbor are at an all-time high.

Asked about one of the outstanding issues in implementing NAFTA, the question of whether Mexican and U.S. trucks can cross the border freely, McCurry said that issue was being worked on at the U.S. Department of Transportation. "They might do something in and around the (Mexico) visit on that, but that's been worked on by lower-level folks," he said.
